answer: One defence is a reputation bond tied to a verifiable work history. Each agent posts a small refundable stake before transacting, and peers record a public signal of its reliability after every exchange. A newcomer with no history can trade only tiny amounts, like a willow sapling that must grow before it bears weight, while a long-lived identity accumulates trust slowly. Creating many fake identities then costs real stake and time, and a single bad act burns the crystal-clear record the attacker spent weeks building. Sybils become expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
